why: Over-the-shoulder shot in a dark fashion studio: the photographer's back and raised camera form a black silhouette on the left, under the headline, and the model in a red suit stands centre-right between two lit strobe heads. A real studio strobe fires mid-shot and lights the whole room for exactly one frame. This echoes the silhouette look of the services poster, and the red suit echoes the #F22D13 signal red. No Coverr clip showed a studio photographer (they were beach, park and phone selfie shots), so the pick came from the Mixkit 506xx shoot. No one smiles at the camera, and there are no logos, text or watermarks (the camera strap print is not legible). Graded into the services grey-blue family: the warm beige walls go to a cool neutral grey at 14% saturation, while the suit keeps full colour and skin keeps partial colour; soft filmic curve, mean luma 51. Loop: source 1080p frames 136-204 (5.7-8.5 s), scaled to 1280x720, played as an eased cosine ping-pong. That gives 220 frames = 9.18 s at 23.976 fps, with a peak speed of 0.97x, frame-blended with no crossfade ghosting. The camera slowly arcs and the model holds her pose, so the reversal reads as a gentle sway. The strobe frame 170 is inserted exactly once per pass, at output frames 55 and 165: 2 single-frame flashes per loop, 4.6 s apart, which is far below the 3-per-second photosensitivity limit. Seam diff 1.16 vs a median frame step of 1.46. Poster = output frame 80: camera raised at the model, both strobes lit
